subject: Territory-binding commitments and operational window ask
messages:
From: Maya Collins <maya.collins@nimbuspay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: NimbusPay Legal <legal@nimbuspay.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:15:00Z
Subject: Territory-binding commitments and operational window ask

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — NimbusPay is keen on Redwood's runtime performance. Before we move to a pilot, our security and legal teams need written commitments on residency and temporary processing windows. Short list of asks below:  

- Can you confirm whether we can get an EU-only pinning guarantee for production workloads (no permanent cross-border egress)?
- What is your defined transient/temporary egress window for failover (hours/days) and how is it instrumented?
- We need a current subprocessors roster, including cloud infra and telemetry providers.
- KMS options: customer-managed keys or escrow for EU-only keys during pinning?
- Access to audit logs (request/response metadata, per-request region) for at least 180 days.

I attached our questionnaire (nimbus_data_residency_questions.xlsx) to help structure answers. We prefer a clear checklist and timeline so we can present to procurement next week.

Can you loop in the legal/ops contacts on your side?

Thanks,
Maya Collins
Head of Security Operations
NimbusPay
[Attachment: nimbus_data_residency_questions.xlsx (Excel, 92 KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Maya Collins <maya.collins@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Territory-binding commitments and operational window ask

Hi Maya — appreciated the clear checklist. Quick responses below and a proposed execution checklist.

Summary answers:
- EU-only pinning: We can provide region pinning for production clusters (EU regions only) with a documented operational SLA; this prevents routine cross-border processing for pinned customers.
- Temporary egress window: Our standard failover window is up to 72 hours for emergency burst replication. We instrument this with automated audit flags + customer notifications; we can reduce to 48 hours on a contract addendum in some cases.
- Subprocessors roster: attached (subprocessors_roster.csv).
- KMS: We offer customer-managed keys (BYOK via KMS) for Dedicated and Private installations; hosted customers can opt into an escrow/escrowed-KMS arrangement for EU-only keys — details in attached DPA.
- Audit logs: Per-request telemetry and region tags are retained 365 days by default; we can scope shorter retention if required.

Proposed execution checklist and timeline (draft):
1) Legal: sign DPA addendum with transient-egress language and explicit pinning clause — target: 7 business days (attachment: redwood_dpa_v3.pdf).
2) Infra: schedule EU cluster provisioning and pinning (estimated 3 business days once DPA executed).
3) KMS: select BYOK or escrow and complete key exchange (up to 5 business days).
4) Ops: enable audit-log exports and shared access (1 business day).
5) Final validation: run a scripted failover test in a staging window and validate logs (1–2 business days).

Please note: permanent cross-border processing (outside EU) will not occur for pinned workloads without explicit written consent. Temporary failover for incident response is limited to the agreed window and will generate an event in the audit stream.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-min call with your legal & ops on Tuesday to walk the DPA addendum and sign-off items? If that's fine I will loop Marissa and Grace who will own legal/ops deliverables on our side.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood_dpa_v3.pdf (PDF, 312 KB), subprocessors_roster.csv (CSV, 24 KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Maya Collins <maya.collins@nimbuspay.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Territory-binding commitments and operational window ask

Hi Maya — copying a few legal clarifications / suggested contract language items for the DPA addendum.

(Quoted from Karthik)
> Permanent cross-border processing (outside EU) will not occur for pinned workloads without explicit written consent. Temporary failover for incident response is limited to the agreed window and will generate an event in the audit stream.

Suggested legal points to include in the DPA addendum:
- Definition: "Transient Processing Window" = automatic replication events required for customer availability during infrastructure incidents; limit default to 72 hours unless otherwise agreed.
- Notification: Redwood will notify customer via email and provide a HubSpot/portal incident link within 2 hours of any cross-border processing event.
- Subprocessor updates: Redwood will provide a 30-day notice for planned subprocessor additions impacting pinned workloads; emergency additions will be disclosed within 7 days with mitigation steps.
- Audit logs: 365 days retention for request/response metadata and region-tagging; any shortened retention must be agreed and reflected in the DPA.
- Law enforcement / disclosure: include standard carve-out; Redwood will challenge overly broad requests and notify customer where lawful and permitted.
- Remedy: material breach of pinning commitments results in rolling back to on-prem or termination rights — subject to cure period.

I've attached a markup of the DPA with the above language flagged (dpa_addendum_markup.docx). We'll keep the operational terms (timelines/ops runbook) in a separate SOW/ops checklist to avoid legal/ops mixing.

Happy to join the Tuesday call to finalize wording.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: dpa_addendum_markup.docx (Word, 48 KB)]

From: Maya Collins <maya.collins@nimbuspay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, NimbusPay Legal <legal@nimbuspay.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Territory-binding commitments and operational window ask

Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed plan. Confirming NimbusPay can accept the proposed approach with the following asks before legal sign-off:  

- One-page executive summary (we'll circulate to procurement).
- Contract language that restricts transient failover to 72 hours by default (we accept 48 hours only if Redwood confirms operational monitoring automation).
- Confirmation that audit logs include a per-request region tag and will be exported to our secure bucket for the pilot.
- Subprocessor roster accepted for pilot scope; long-term additions will follow the 30-day notice.

We'll take the DPA markup to our legal team today. Let's book the Tuesday 30-min call (May 11) at 10:00 CET for sign-off and SOW sequencing.
